case_reference.focal_claim: there was a … decline in the temperature-mortality relationship across decades (p. 133.)
case_reference.hypothesis: The relationship between temperature and mortality declined across decades, with a weaker association in later periods than in earlier periods.

tasks_info.task_instruction: Conduct the analysis without any restrictions.

You should use 90 °F as a threshold for temperature extremes. You should compute the decline between the 1931–59 and 1960–2004 periods. You should conduct your analysis without geographical, or precipitation frequency specification of the data. You should use a 2 months temperature exposure window in your analysis. You should disregard socio-economic factors and technological and public health advancements over time in your analysis. You should not specify the causes of death in your analysis.

planning_output.path_summary: The proposed path uses the original DATA_1900_2004.dta panel data to test whether the temperature-mortality relationship declined over time. Task1 constructs state-month, year-month, quadratic year, decade, two-period decade, and below-40-degree variables; drops observations with missing lndrate; restricts the sample to years 1931 and later; then estimates OLS regressions of lndrate on temperature-bin days and interactions with either factor(decade_two) or factor(decade), including population-age-share, income, state-month, year-month, quadratic time, and precipitation controls. Task2 uses the same cleaned 1931-2004 sample but follows the restriction to use only days above 90 °F, compares 1931-1959 with 1960-2004, and omits socioeconomic, geographical, and precipitation-frequency controls.

path_signature.main_predictor: Task1: temperature-bin-day variables b10_1, b10_2, b10_3, b10_4, b10_5, b10_6, b10_8, b10_9, b10_10 and selected extreme bins b10_9, b10_10, b10_b_4 interacted with factor(decade_two) or factor(decade). Task2: b10_10 interacted with factor(decade_two).
path_signature.sample_restriction: Drop rows with missing lndrate and keep observations with year >= 1931.
path_signature.variable_construction: statemo = stfips * 1000 + month; yearmo = year * 1000 + month; year2 = year^2; b10_b_4 = b10_1 + b10_2 + b10_3 + b10_4; decade is coded as ten-year categories from 1900-1909 through 2000-2004; decade_two = 1 for year <= 1959 and 2 for year > 1959.
path_signature.inference_rule: Evaluate the interaction coefficients between temperature exposure bins and period or decade indicators. Evidence for the claim is a negative interaction indicating a weaker temperature-mortality association in later decades or in 1960-2004 relative to 1931-1959.

preprocessing_steps: For Task1, compute b10_b_4 as the sum of b10_1 through b10_4.
For Task1, compute decade as a categorical ten-year period variable.
For both tasks, compute decade_two as 1 for years up to 1959 and 2 for years after 1959.
Restrict the analytic sample to years 1931 through 2004.
outputs: Interaction plots of lndrate against temperature-bin variables by decade or two-period decade category.

planning_output.method_justification: The claim concerns a decline in the temperature-mortality relationship across time. The proposed OLS models directly estimate mortality as a function of temperature exposure bins and test whether the temperature slope differs by decade or by the pre-1959 versus post-1959 period. Negative interaction terms for later decades or for the 1960-2004 period indicate a decline in the temperature-mortality relationship. Task2 follows the required specification by using b10_10 as the 90 °F threshold variable and comparing 1931-1959 with 1960-2004 without geographical, precipitation-frequency, socioeconomic, technological, public-health, or cause-of-death specifications.
